posts.author: Jeffrey Weil
posts.content_md:
Hello Steve_rb

I'm Jeffrey Weil pres. of NorthBeach Holography. I suggest you do not get this embosser. I looked at the page and the " Narrow Web Hard hologram Embosser Mold 2" is a machine thats produced here in America and they are just reselling. I would think other equipment they are selling is also not made there

You will also probably get better support and spare part availability by buying a machine from the states or from western Europe anyway. 

The rollers are also not the type you would want to have.

If you want to set up a production line I suggest you get a consultant to help out. This is not a turnkey thing. You won't get far without instructions on how to use the new equipment. If your interested my company does these "technology transfers" and can get you set up quickly. 

I can set you up with the full package. Mastering, electroforming, embossing, die cutting, etc.....

posts.author: Jeffrey Weil
posts.content_md:
Hello Steve_rb,

The rollers on that machine are "hard" Just d5 hardened steel highly polished. The more advanced rollers are "soft" they have a layer of a fancy polymer that allows the rollers to conform to each other and the shim. 

This allows you to make "flat" shims. For hard rollers you need to make "crowned" ones. Much harder to do and to tweak out to each machine.

A crowned shim has been made through a series of apertures that leave the shim with a complex cross section that has different areas of the shim being different thicknesses. After its been run a few feet it flattens out to the right shape for a nice emboss across the rollers. 

A flat shim has no apertures in front of it during the electroforming process so it just grows in a regular slight parabolic shape. During embossing the rollers conform to the needed shape for a nice emboss across the machines width.

 Jeffrey Weil

 NorthBeach Holography
